kicker: An agent built for little attention

scenes.headline: How an agent decides when to bother you
scenes.sub: A gate, a ticket, a worker, a panel
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Docket! This agent works through a repository's issues and pull requests. Here is how it decides who may ask, and when to speak up.

scenes.text: Who may start work is a small table a person can read, not a prompt. The model only judges what the table lets through.
scenes.mark: a small table a person can read
scenes.say: Who may start work is a small table a person can read. The model only judges what the table lets through.

scenes.title: From a message to a pull request

steps.say: A message arrives. The gate checks who sent it and whether it addressed the agent.
Only an admitted message reaches the model, which must judge every written rule exactly once.
An accept creates a ticket that records why the work is allowed, and how far it may go.
The ticket gets its own worker session and directory, and the result comes back as a pull request.

left.title: Anyone, then judge
left.say: The usual way sends every message to the model, so clever phrasing can change what is allowed.

right.title: Gate first
items: A table decides who can ask
right.say: Here a table decides first. With the default table, an unlisted person never makes an explicit request.

scenes.label: worker slots by default, plus one for a person
scenes.say: By default three workers run at once. A person's message gets one extra slot, so new work never blocks a reply.

scenes.text: Put who may start work in a table you can read, and let the agent speak only when a person must act.
scenes.say: Put who may start work in a table you can read, and let the agent speak only when a person must act.

recap: A gate decides who may ask
Each ticket gets its own worker
Workers run as you, so isolate them
scenes.say: A gate decides who may ask. Each ticket gets its own worker. And the workers run as you, so give them their own account.
